results.name: Chin Up Reverse Close Grip
instructions: Begin by grasping a pull-up bar with a close underhand grip (palms facing you) and your hands placed closer than shoulder-width apart. Hang with your arms fully extended and your legs slightly bent or crossed behind you.
Engage your back and start pulling your body upward by bending your elbows and contracting your biceps, continuing until your chin is above the bar.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with a controlled movement, fully extending your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your biceps and upper back muscles to lift your body, avoiding excessive momentum.
Perform the movement slowly and with control, especially during the lowering phase, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
Use a full range of motion by fully extending your arms at the bottom and bringing your chin above the bar at the top.
results.description: Chin Up Reverse Close Grip is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Chin-Up (Isometric and Negative)
instructions: Begin by grasping a pull-up bar with an underhand grip (palms facing you) and your hands shoulder-width apart. Hang with your arms fully extended and your legs slightly bent or crossed behind you.
Engage your core and pull your shoulder blades down and back to start the movement.
Pull your body upward by bending your elbows and contracting your biceps, continuing until your chin is above the bar. Hold this top position (isometric hold) for a specified duration.
After the hold, slowly lower yourself back to the starting position (negative phase), taking about 3-5 seconds to fully extend your arms. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your biceps and upper back muscles to lift your body, avoiding excessive momentum.
Perform the isometric hold with control, ensuring your muscles are engaged and you are not simply hanging from the bar.
During the negative phase, lower yourself slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
results.description: Chin-Up (Isometric and Negative) is an intermediate multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the biceps (upper arms). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Commando Pull-Up
instructions: Begin by grasping a pull-up bar with both hands placed close together, palms facing each other in a neutral grip.
Hang with your arms fully extended and your body straight.
Engage your back and pull your body up towards the bar, leaning your head to one side of the bar as you lift.
Lower yourself back to the starting position with a controlled movement. Repeat the pull-up, alternating the side of your head relative to the bar for each repetition.
tips: Use a full range of motion by fully extending your arms at the bottom and bringing your head above the bar at the top.
Perform the movement slowly and with control, especially during the lowering phase, to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you pull up and inhaling as you lower yourself.
results.description: Commando Pull-Up is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Dumbbell Alternating Pendlay Row
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder width apart and hold a dumbbell in each hand. Bend your knees and hinge forward at your hips until your torso is nearly parallel to the floor, allowing both arms to hang straight beneath your shoulders, resting the dumbbells on the floor.
Pull one dumbbell toward your abdomen by driving your elbow upward close to your body, while keeping the opposite arm extended.
Lower the dumbbell back to the starting position with control until your arm is fully extended.
Repeat the movement with the opposite arm, alternating sides while maintaining the bent-over position throughout the exercise.
tips: Keep your back flat and your chest facing the floor throughout the movement.
Brace your core to prevent your torso from rotating as you row.
Maintain a neutral neck by looking toward the floor a few feet in front of you.
Inhale as you lower the dumbbell and exhale as you pull it upward.
results.description: Dumbbell Alternating Pendlay Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Shoulders, Core.

results.name: Dumbbell Bent Arm Pullover
instructions: Lie perpendicular on a bench with only your upper back supported and your hips slightly lowered. Hold a dumbbell with both hands above your chest, keeping your elbows slightly bent.
Engage your core and keep your feet flat on the floor for stability. Slowly lower the dumbbell in an arc over your head, maintaining the slight bend in your elbows.
Lower the dumbbell until your upper arms are in line with your torso or as far as comfortable, feeling a stretch in your chest and lats.
Pull the dumbbell back to the starting position with a controlled motion, keeping your elbows slightly bent. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid letting your elbows flare out; maintain a slight bend throughout the movement.
Ensure your shoulders and upper back remain in contact with the bench throughout the exercise.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize muscle engagement and prevent injury.
results.description: Dumbbell Bent Arm Pullover is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Triceps.
